---

## Convergent Signal

Four sources point at the same regime on the same day:
1. April PPI: highest monthly print since March 2022, broadening beyond energy
2. April Retail Sales: strongest annual gain since August 2025 despite record-low consumer sentiment
3. 10Y Treasury at 4.47%: highest close since August 2025; term premium at 35bps and rising

|---|---|---|---|---|

|---|---|---|

- UMich consumer sentiment: at record lows (who are they surveying?)
- Actual control group spending: rising
- Read: aggregate spending resilient because upper-income households are ~50% of spending; wealth effects (equities at ATH), AI-driven income gains, and gas-price normalization are insulating the top half of the distribution
- Risk: if tech/equity wealth effect reverses, the top-income spending floor disappears rapidly

---

|---|---|---|

| 30Y yield | **5.03%** | Above 5% for first time in auction since 2007 |
| Term premium vs fair value | **+35bps** | Capital Spectator estimate; was near 0 in late 2025 |
| UK 30Y gilt | **5.74%** | Highest since 1997 — contagion channel |

| BoJ 10Y JGB | Highest since 1997 | Masu hawkish; June hike probability rising |

The term premium reset from near-zero to 35bps in 4 months is the story. The prior regime (2025 late) was defined by the premium fading after the 2021-2022 inflation spike. - Markets: 40% probability of a Fed hike by year-end (pricing up significantly post-PPI)

**Key regime signal:** If the Fed pivots from "cuts coming" to "hike if broadening continues," the duration trade inverts and equity multiple expansion becomes a de facto short. The AI earnings case must carry more weight.

> "When value and growth can't agree on who's in charge for more than a session, the market is telling you the regime is changing. Watch breadth, watch bond yields, and don't mistake daily noise for direction. The rotation itself is the signal."

- Late 1999 → 2000: value outperformed in stretches during dot-com wobble, then growth surged to final high before permanent reversal
- 2007: financial sector oscillation through spring as credit cracks showed
- Late 2021 → early 2022: mega-cap growth flip-flopped before Fed pivot crushed growth for 9 months

**This does not guarantee a bear market.** But it does signal the regime consensus has fractured — investors no longer agree on the direction of liquidity, rates, or earnings. Daily rotation is the market searching for a new leadership structure.

## Watchpoint 1 — August 12 Tariff Cliff

| 90-day China tariff pause expiry | August 12, 2026 — pause ends unless renewed or replaced with framework | Track White House / USTR press releases; watch Bloomberg tariff tracker; set calendar alert for July 15 (30-day pre-alert) | If no framework by July 15: prepare fresh entry in defensive/domestic-revenue names; avoid new entry in China-exposed US multinationals |

**Background:** Goldman's base case is a ceasefire — both sides step back from their most aggressive postures and extend the pause, possibly indefinitely. The structural problem is that Trump's tariff authority was struck down, leaving the administration with slower mechanisms. China knows this.

# El Niño 2026 Commodity Risk Watchpoints (2026-05-14)

*NOAA gives a 61% probability of El Niño conditions emerging by May–July 2026, with a 25% probability of a super El Niño (>2°C). The 1997/98 super El Niño is the historical benchmark. Arriving on top of an active Iran-Hormuz oil shock, a super El Niño would be a second simultaneous commodity supply shock — compounding inflation, disrupting agricultural output, and extending the energy crisis timeline.*

---

## Current Conditions

| Signal | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Global ocean surface temps (April 2026) | 21°C — 2nd warmest April on record | Copernicus Climate Change Service |
| El Niño emergence probability (May–July) | **61%** | NOAA Climate Prediction Center |
| Super El Niño probability (>2°C, winter peak) | **25%** | NOAA CPC |
| La Niña end | January 2026 — fastest transition on record | NOAA / LiveScience |
| Met Office assessment | "One of the most significant El Niño events this century, comparable to 1997/98" | UK Met Office |
| NOAA confidence | Unusually high for spring (spring predictability barrier typically reduces confidence) | NOAA |
| 2026 expected to rank as | 2nd warmest year on record; 2027 potentially warmest ever (Carbon Brief) | Carbon Brief |

---

## Historical Benchmark: 1997/98 Super El Niño

| Phase | Duration | Peak Anomaly | Market Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1997/98 | 13 three-month periods (May 1997 – June 1998) | +2.4°C | Global agricultural disruption, flooding/drought patterns, fishery collapse |
| 2015/16 | 20 three-month periods | +2.8°C peak (but weaker in eastern Pacific) | Commodity shock, coral bleaching, Australia/SE Asia drought |

If 2026 El Niño reaches the super threshold (>2°C), impacts include: fishery collapse (Peruvian anchovy/salmon), Australian drought and wildfires, SE Asian flooding, California/US Southwest rainfall disruption, and global agricultural output disruption across multiple crops.

---

## Commodity Transmission Channels

| Commodity | El Niño Effect | Compounding Factor | Portfolio Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Corn / Soybeans | US Midwest wetter-than-normal → potential yield boost; SE Asia drought → palm oil stress | Iran-Hormuz urea/fertilizer shock already active | Watch: WASDE revisions; Purdue [[Ag Economy Barometer]] |
| Wheat | Australia and southern hemisphere crop risk | Hormuz already disrupted Black Sea substitution flows | ALERT if wheat futures +15%+ above prior year |
| Coffee / Cocoa | Brazil drought risk (El Niño typically dries out east Brazil) | Already stressed by prior La Niña cycle | Watch: softs futures |
| Fisheries / Marine proteins | Peruvian anchoveta fishery collapse → anchovy meal → fishmeal/feed cost spike | — | Watch: poultry/aquaculture input cost pass-through |
| Energy — LNG | SE Asian demand spike (cooling); Australian LNG export disruption risk | Qatar Ras Laffan already damaged by Iran-war strikes | ALERT: TTF/JKM spike potential; Europe winter storage risk |
| Energy — Hydro | Brazilian hydro disruption → natgas backup demand | Global natgas tight from Hormuz | Watch: Brazilian power sector stress |
| Insurance / Cat bonds | Wildfire (Australia/California), flooding (SE Asia), cyclone risk | — | Watch: reinsurance pricing |

---

## Watchpoint Table

| Watch Item | Signal Threshold | Scanner / Alert Criteria | Opportunity When Fired |
|---|---|---|---|
| El Niño officially declared | NOAA 3-month running mean ONI ≥ +0.5°C for 5 overlapping periods | Monthly NOAA ENSO Advisory (released ~mid-month); ONI index | WATCH: begin monitoring agricultural commodity setups |
| Super El Niño confirmed (>2°C) | NOAA ONI peak anomaly forecast > +2.0°C | NOAA seasonal forecast update; ECMWF model ensemble | ALERT: agricultural commodity watchpoints activate; energy LNG premium watchpoint activates |
| Australian drought signal | Bureau of Meteorology rainfall deficit >25% across east Australia | BoM monthly climate outlook | ALERT: wheat/cotton/dairy supply shock; Australian equity agricultural sector |
| SE Asia flooding | Sustained above-normal rainfall across Philippines/Indonesia/Vietnam | NOAA CPC tropical monitoring | ALERT: palm oil supply disruption; LNG export disruption |
| US Midwest corn belt wet | Above-normal spring precipitation forecast for Iowa/Illinois | USDA crop progress weekly reports | WATCH: corn yield upside potential — may partially offset global ag shock |
| LNG Japan/Korea premium spike | JKM premium vs TTF above prior seasonal range | ICE JKM futures monitor | ALERT: Asia competition for European LNG storage capacity |

---

## Compounding Risk Assessment

| Scenario | Probability | Key Impact |
|---|---|---|
| El Niño develops, stays moderate (<1.5°C) | ~35% | Minor commodity disruption; energy markets absorb |
| Strong El Niño (1.5–2.0°C) | ~25% | Significant agricultural disruption; LNG demand spike; inflation persistence |
| Super El Niño (>2°C) | ~25% | Multi-quarter agricultural shock on top of Iran energy shock; global food CPI acceleration; central bank forced hand; 1997/98 analogue |
| No El Niño / fizzles | ~15% | Ocean temps revert; existing Hormuz/inflation dynamic continues alone |

**Base case is Strong El Niño.** The super El Niño scenario (25%) is not the base but is not negligible — and the compounding effect with the ongoing Iran-Hormuz energy shock makes it a portfolio-relevant tail that is not being priced.

---

## Trade Expression Layer

| Layer | Read |
|---|---|
| Regime | [[Macro/Regimes/Iran-Hormuz Oil Shock]] + [[Macro/Regimes/Inflationary Boom]] |
| Directional thesis | Super El Niño compounds Iran energy shock → second simultaneous commodity supply disruption → inflation persistence |
| Strategy family | Agricultural commodity long / energy (LNG) long / commodity producer equity / inflation hedge |
| Technical confirmation | El Niño officially declared + first regional drought signal (Australia or SE Asia) |
| Volatility / options overlay | Agricultural vol (CBOT corn options, wheat options); LNG options if available; soft commodity ETF options |
| Expression candidates | CORN, WEAT, DBA commodity ETFs; agricultural producer equities; LNG shipper equities; reinsurance underperformance short |
| Invalidation | El Niño fizzles (NOAA reforecast below 0.5°C threshold); OR Iran resolution restores agricultural commodity flows independently |
| Next data pull | NOAA ENSO Advisory (monthly, mid-month); WASDE; BoM Australia seasonal outlook; Purdue Ag Economy Barometer |

### Expression Notes
- Do not position on El Niño risk until NOAA officially declares; probability is elevated but not confirmed.
- The Iran-Hormuz agriculture channel (fertilizer, shipping) is already active — El Niño adds a second layer, not a substitute.
